blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: In a Benders loop, one region's staffing LP has no feasible solution for the plan the master just proposed, and the LP solver returns no dual ray. What should the loop add to the master?

options.text: An optimality cut from the infeasible LP's duals, built as for a feasible year
options.says: An infeasible LP has no optimal duals; the page builds the cut from a shortfall LP instead.

options.text: A feasibility cut from a dual ray, which GLOP returns for an infeasible LP
options.says: In the lesson's run GLOP returned no dual ray for an infeasible LP.

options.text: A feasibility cut from a shortfall LP's duals, refusing plans short the same way
options.says: Right: the shortfall LP is feasible for every plan, and its duals give a cut valid for every plan.

options.text: Skip the year: the next master solve proposes a different plan on its own
options.says: Nothing in the master forbids the plan, so the master can propose it again; it needs a row that forbids it.

origin.section: An Infeasible Year Returns a Feasibility Cut From a Shortfall LP

questions.stem: A Benders loop for a maximization is stopped after 4 iterations by a deadline. The master's last value is 51,800; the best proposed plan whose every subproblem was feasible is worth 51,200 at its true value. What can be reported?

options.text: The optimum is 51,800, the master's value; the master's last plan is the one to use
options.says: The master is a relaxation: its value is an upper bound, and its plan's true value may be lower.

options.text: The optimum lies above 51,800, since the master gains rows; use the master's plan
options.says: Adding rows can only lower a maximization's master value, so 51,800 is an upper bound.

options.text: The optimum lies below 51,200, since the cuts lower values; use the 51,200 plan
options.says: The 51,200 plan is feasible, so the optimum is at least 51,200.

options.text: The optimum lies between 51,200 and 51,800; the 51,200 plan is the one to use
options.says: Right: the master's value is an upper bound and the feasible plan's true value a lower bound.

origin.section: The Master Is an Upper Bound, Each Plan's True Value a Lower Bound; Stop When They Meet

questions.stem: A team moves its Benders loop into one branch-and-bound search: the cut function is registered as a lazy-constraint callback, and the master is solved with HiGHS through MathOpt. The solve reports OPTIMAL at a value above the loop's answer. What happened?

options.text: HiGHS called the callback too often, so it sent cuts for plans it had pruned
options.says: HiGHS through MathOpt never called the callback at all (lesson 4.3.5 shows it).

options.text: HiGHS did not call the callback, so its plan breaks cuts it was not sent
options.says: Right: HiGHS accepts the registration and ignores it; the master then believes crews are free.

options.text: The lazy cuts are weaker than the loop's, so one search stops at a higher value
options.says: The same cut function, sent to SCIP in one search, reached the loop's optimum, 23,812.25, so the cuts are not weaker.

options.text: The loop stopped early, so its answer is below the one search's true optimum
options.says: The loop's two bounds met at 23,812.25, the monolithic MILP's value, so it did not stop early.

origin.section: HiGHS Cannot Take the Cuts Inside Its Search; SCIP Can, as Lazy Constraints
